title: Named-roots view item-lifecycle reads: stop on client abandonment, keep the batch within the shared permit's bound, and test the route's limiter wiring
outcome: Named-roots view item-lifecycle reads: stop on client abandonment, keep the batch within the shared permit's bound, and test the route's limiter wiring
acceptance: GET /api/engram/named-roots stops launching item-lifecycle reads once its client has gone (the WorkReadAbandonGuard / work_read_not_abandoned pattern of the other Work-read routes); the remaining rows show an unknown reason

The item-lifecycle batch holds a shared WORK_READ_PERMITS permit no longer than the bound other Work views size their admission wait to (ENGRAM_WORK_BINDING_COMMAND_TIMEOUT), or the difference is documented with its reason

A route-level test drives list_engram_named_roots with a private WorkReadLimiter: with no permits every row shows 'unknown (tracker reads busy)', and with one permit the permit is free again after the response and itemLifecycle is serialized on the wire
